changes_under_test.gate (br-v0ucm): db pool.rs WalResetGate: DbPool::acquire waits (bounded 2 s) while closed. queries.rs commit_tx: when the post-commit PASSIVE checkpoint is refused and the WAL exceeds journal_size_limit (min 1 MiB), close the gate, retry a zero-wait PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) every 1 ms until in-flight transactions drain (250 ms budget, 1 s cooldown on failure), reopen; a truncate also publishes the commit so the connection is kept.
changes_under_test.9bwnb (br-9bwnb): storage lib.rs: reservation artifacts written + fdatasynced under .tmp-* names outside ARCHIVE_PUBLICATION_FENCE; the fence covers only the renames.

attribution: Paced 60-agent load on the 9bwnb build with commit_tx debug tracing: 100% of contended post-commit checkpoints return busy=1 checkpointed=0 (fsqlite-core 0.4.10 refuses any checkpoint while a concurrent transaction is active). The WAL reset only in idle gaps (17-32 MB) until load became continuous at ~140 s, then grew ~1 MB/s to 322 MB; every retired-and-reopened connection rescans it.
decision_rule_predeclared_2026_10_10T11_: gate9 vs base WIN iff in BOTH rounds reservation p50 and p90 >= 2x better, last-60s send p90 <= 2x base, errors not higher; gate vs base no-regression: p50/p90 within +25%; gate9 vs patched: last-window send p90 drops, WAL peak < 64 MB.

verdict:
WIN under the predeclared paced rule, with one new red release-smoke check that is explained below. These are equal-offered-load results (60 agents, one iteration every 6 s, 300 s, two mirrored rounds, same invocation).
- gate9 vs base: reservation p50 0.169/0.166 s vs 11.16/10.73 s; reservation p90 2.50/3.49 s vs 14.95/15.51 s; send p90 in the last 60 s 0.21/0.22 s vs 0.25/0.20 s; WAL peak 17.0/16.7 MB vs 30.6/27.7 MB; errors 1/2 vs 1/3, all immediate.
- The gate alone is latency-neutral (every p50/p90 within +4% of base) and halves the WAL peak.
- 9bwnb alone reproduces the 8-11 s send flip (last-60 s send p90 9.10/11.25 s, WAL 191/250 MB). The gate removes the flip.
- Cost: gate9's overall send p90 is 0.40 vs 0.30-0.32 s and its send p99 is 2.4-3.6 vs 1.5 s. All of it falls in the first minute.

Release smoke, both orders (closed loop):
- The swarm phase completes 6668 sends vs 3500-3696, with send p99 4.10-4.18 s vs 4.14-4.83 s (both under 5 s).
- Reservation p50 is 4.6-4.9 s vs 12.5-13.2 s. p99 is 14.6 s vs 22.3-24.1 s, so both arms still fail the 5 s bound. The remaining tail is the WBQ drain holding the fence through message-bundle fsyncs (br-kp1in.13).
- Tool errors are the same rate in both arms (RESOURCE_BUSY 5 in ~17k calls vs 3 in ~9k). There are zero 30 s dispatch timeouts, every acknowledged send survives SIGKILL, and integrity_check is ok.
- NEW RED: in the soak phase, gate9 completes 5110-5158 sends vs 1759-2041. The check 'WBQ drained_total advances in every 10s window with queued work' then fails in both orders, while base passes it. The drain is not stuck. It writes 2.5x more artifacts (archive 5674 vs 2261, converged after load), and health's own stall verdict agrees with the counters. drained_total is bumped once per drain batch, and at 3x input the batches outlast the 10 s window. This is archive lag under higher throughput. The check is unchanged. A follow-up bead tracks it with br-kp1in.13.
